bibl.title: La rappresentazione del palazzo di Cleopatra in Lucano, Bellum civile X.
bibl.seg: Nicola Lanzarone, La rappresentazione del palazzo di Cleopatra in Lucano, Bellum civile X.
bibl.note: Deals with Lucan's description of Cleopatra's palace in Bellum civile 10. It fits into the epic tradition of representations of royal palaces, which dates back to Homer, Odyssey 7 (ekphrasis of the palace of Alcinous), although Lucan's main terms of comparison are Catullus 64 (the palace of Peleus) and, above all, Virgil, Aeneid 1 (the palace of Dido). Lucan departs from this tradition in his undeniably hyperbolic representation of the Egyptian palace and its unparalleled luxury.
